**Allah the Exalted said: ﴿that you should say﴾ is in the accusative position (fi mawdi' nasb). The Kufans (al-Kufiyyun, the grammarians of Kufa) said: "It means: lest you say." The Basrans (al-Basriyyun, the grammarians of Basra) said: "We sent it down out of dislike that you would say." Al-Farra' and al-Kisa'i said: "The meaning is: beware that you say, O people of Makkah."**

(Innama unzila al-kitab) means the Torah and the Gospel.

(Ala ta'ifatayn min qablina) means upon the Jews and the Christians, and no Book was sent down to us.

(Wa in kunna 'an dirasatihim laghafilin) means: we were unaware of reciting their books and of their languages. He did not say "'an dirasatihima" (their two studies), because each group (ta'ifah) is a collective noun (jama'ah).

(Aw taqulu) is conjoined to "an taqulu."

(Fa-qad ja'akum bayyinatun min rabbikum) means: the excuse has been removed by the coming of Muhammad (ﷺ). Al-bayyinah and al-bayan are one and the same, and what is meant is Muhammad (ﷺ), whom Allah, glorified is He, named a bayyinah (clear proof).

(Wa huda wa rahmah) means: for whoever follows him. Then He said: (Fa-man azlamu) means: so if you deny, then no one is more wrongdoing than you.

**Sadafa** (to turn away, to avoid) and **yasdifun** (they turn away, they avoid). This has already been discussed (see vol. 6, p. 428).

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 158 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Do they await anything?﴾ Its meaning is: I have established the proof against them and sent down the Book to them, yet they did not believe, so what are they waiting for?

(﴿Do they await anything but that the angels come to them?﴾) That is, at death, to seize their souls.

(﴿Or that your Lord comes?﴾) Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak said: "Your Lord's command concerning them, by killing or otherwise." The genitive complement is sometimes mentioned while what is meant is the thing it is attached to, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And ask the town﴾ [[See vol. 9, p. 245.]], meaning the people of the town. And His saying: ﴿and they were made to drink the calf into their hearts﴾ [[See vol. 2, p. 31.]], meaning the love of the calf. Likewise here: ﴿the command of your Lord comes﴾, that is, the punishment of your Lord and the chastisement of your Lord. It is also said that this is among the ambiguous (al-mutashabih, verses whose true meaning is known only to God) that none knows its interpretation except God. The discussion of its like has preceded in al-Baqarah and elsewhere.

(﴿Or that some of the signs of your Lord come﴾) It is said: this is the rising of the sun from its west. By this it is made clear that they are given respite in the world, and when the Hour appears there is no respite.

It is also said: the coming of God, Exalted is He, is His arrival to decide the judgment among His creatures at the standing place of the Resurrection, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank﴾ [[The text reads: "وجاء ربك والملك صفا" ]]. His arrival, Exalted is He, is not movement, nor transfer, nor cessation, for that occurs only when the one who comes is a body or a substance. What the majority of the imams of Ahl al-Sunnah (the people of the Sunnah, the orthodox majority) hold is that they say: He comes, He descends, and He arrives, without asking how, for ﴿there is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [[See vol. 16, p. 7.]].

In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Three things, when they come forth, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before or had not earned good through its faith: the rising of the sun from its west, the Dajjal (the Antichrist), and the Beast of the earth." And from Safwan ibn 'Assal al-Muradi, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: "Indeed in the west there is a door, open for repentance, the distance of seventy years in breadth, which is not closed until the sun rises from its direction." Al-Daraqutni and al-Darimi recorded it, and al-Tirmidhi, who said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Sufyan [[Sufyan: one of the narrators in the chain of this hadith.]] said: "Towards Syria; God created it on the day He created the heavens and the earth." (Open) means for repentance, which is not closed until the sun rises from it. He said: "A hasan sahih hadith."

I say: the Khawarij (a sect that rejected the caliphate of 'Ali and held extreme views on sin) denied all of this, and so did the Mu'tazilah (a rationalist theological school), as has preceded. [[If he means the Ibadiyyah, as he claims, then stoning is established among them as a binding ruling until the Day of Resurrection, but as a sunnah, as is authentically reported in the Musnad of al-Rabi' from Abu al-Sha'tha' Jabir ibn Zayd, not from the Qur'an. They have continued to stone in their imamate, and they did not deny the rising of the sun from the west or the emergence of the Dajjal.]]

Ibn 'Abbas narrated, who said: I heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab say [[Thus in the originals, except in K: "yaqulu" (he says). What is in al-Durr al-Manthur reads: "... 'Umar addressed us and said."]]: "O people, indeed stoning is true, so do not be deceived about it. The sign of that is that the Messenger of God ﷺ stoned, and Abu Bakr stoned, and we stoned after them both. There will come a people from this Ummah who deny stoning, deny the Dajjal, deny the rising of the sun from its west, deny the punishment of the grave, deny intercession, and deny a people who will come out of the Fire after they have been burned." Abu 'Umar mentioned it. [[Amtahashu: were burned. Al-mahsh: the skin burns and the bone shows. It is also transmitted in the passive form, "umtahishu".]]

Al-Tha'labi mentioned, in a lengthy hadith, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, something to the effect that: the sun is held back from the people when sins multiply on the earth, good is lost so that no one enjoins it, and wrongdoing spreads so that no one forbids it, for the length of a night beneath the Throne. Each time it prostrates and asks its Lord, Exalted is He, from where it should rise, no answer comes to it [[In Y and Z: "yakhruj" (come out). In B: "fala yuhar ilayha" (no one returns to it).]], until the moon meets it and prostrates with it, and they ask from where they should rise, and no answer comes to them [[In Z: "yujab" (answered). In B and K: "yuhar" (perplexed).]], until the two are held back for three nights for the sun and two nights for the moon. No one knows the length of that night except those who pray at night in the earth, and they are on that day a small band in every town of the Muslim lands. When the period of three nights is complete for them, God, Exalted is He, sends Gabriel, peace be upon him, to them, and he says: "Indeed the Lord, glorified and exalted, commands you both to return to your wests, and rise from it, and there is no light for you with us, nor any radiance." So they rise from their wests dark, with no light for the sun nor radiance for the moon, like their state in their eclipse before that. That is His saying: ﴿and the sun and the moon are joined﴾ [[See vol. 19, pp. 94 and 225.]] and His saying: ﴿when the sun is folded up﴾ [[See vol. 19, pp. 94 and 225.]]. Then they rise like two camels yoked together, until, when the sun and the moon reach the middle of the sky, Gabriel, peace be upon him [[From Z and K.]], comes to them, takes hold of their horns, and turns them back to the west. He does not set them from their wests but sets them from the door of repentance, then returns the two leaves of the door, and what is between them is joined so that it is as if there had never been a split between them. When the door of repentance is closed, no repentance will be accepted from a servant after that, and no good deed he does will benefit him after that, except one who was already a doer of good before that day, for he will continue to receive what he had before that day. That is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith﴾. Then the sun and the moon are clothed again after that with light and radiance, then they rise over the people and set as they used to rise and set before that.

The scholars said: The reason that faith does not benefit a soul when the sun rises from the west is that fear reaches their hearts to such a degree that every appetite of the soul goes out, and every power of the body becomes weak. So all people, through their certainty of the nearness of the Resurrection, come to be in the state of one present at death, in that the motives to the various kinds of sins are cut off from them and their bodies are rendered inert. Whoever repents in such a state, his repentance is not accepted, just as the repentance of one present at death is not accepted. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed God accepts the repentance of the servant so long as he has not begun the death rattle" [[That is, his soul has not reached the top of his throat. This is the time of direct witnessing, in which he sees his seat in Paradise or his seat in the Fire. So the one who witnesses the rising of the sun from its west is like him.]]. And on this basis, the repentance of everyone who witnesses that, or who is as one witnessing it, should be rejected for as long as he lives, because his knowledge of God, of His Prophet ﷺ, and of His promise has become necessary knowledge. But if the days of the world are prolonged until people forget this great matter, and speak of it only a little, so that the report of it becomes restricted and its mass transmission is cut off, then whoever embraces Islam at that time or repents will be accepted from him. And God knows best.

In Sahih Muslim, from 'Abd Allah [ibn Mas'ud], who said: I memorized from the Messenger of God ﷺ a hadith that I have not forgotten since. I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: "Indeed the first of the signs to come out is the rising of the sun from its west, and the coming out of the Beast upon the people in the forenoon, and whichever of them occurs before the other, the other will follow it soon after." And in it, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was in an upper chamber while we were below him. He looked down at us and said: "What are you mentioning?" We said: "The Hour." He said: "Indeed the Hour will not come until there are ten signs: an earthquake in the east, an earthquake in the west, an earthquake in the Arabian Peninsula, the smoke, the Dajjal, the Beast of the earth, Gog and Magog, the rising of the sun from its west, and a fire that comes out from the bottom of 'Aden and drives people on." Shu'bah said: "And 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Rufay' narrated to me from Abu al-Tufayl, from Abu Sarihah, the like of that, without mentioning the Prophet ﷺ." One of them said, regarding the tenth: "And the descent of 'Isa ibn Maryam ﷺ." The other said: "And a wind that casts people into the sea."

I say: this is a sound hadith (mutqan) regarding the order of the signs. Some of them have occurred, namely the earthquakes, as Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi mentioned, that they occurred in Iraq of the non-Arabs and in the Maghrib, and a great multitude perished because of them, as he mentioned in his book Fuhum al-Athar and elsewhere. The mention of the Beast comes in al-Naml [[See vol. 13, p. 234.]], and of Gog and Magog in al-Kahf [[See vol. 11, p. 55.]]. It is said that the signs follow one another like beads strung on a thread, one after another.

It is also said that the ruling concerning the rising of the sun from the west is that Abraham, peace be upon him, said to Nimrod: "Indeed God brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west," and the one who disbelieved was confounded [[See vol. 3, p. 283.]]. And that the atheists and the astrologers, all of them, deny this and say: "It is not going to happen." So God, Exalted is He, will make the sun rise from the west one day, to show the deniers His power, that the sun is in His dominion: if He wills, He makes it rise from the east, and if He wills, He makes it rise from the west.

On this basis it is possible that the rejection of repentance and faith applies to those who, among the deniers of that, believe and repent, while they had denied the Prophet's ﷺ report of its rising. As for those who affirm it, their repentance is accepted, and their faith benefits them as it did before that.

It is related from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas that he said: No deed or repentance is accepted from an unbeliever [[In K: "his faith, nor his repentance, nor his deed."]] when he embraces Islam at the time he sees it, except one who was a child on that day, for if he embraced Islam after that, it would be accepted from him. And one who was a believer and a sinner, if he repents from the sin, it is accepted from him.

It is related from 'Imran ibn Husayn that he said: His repentance was not accepted only at the time of the rising of the sun, when there is a cry in which many people perish. So whoever embraces Islam or repents at that time and then dies, his repentance is not accepted, but whoever repents after that, his repentance is accepted. Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi mentioned it in his tafsir.

'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: People will remain after the rising of the sun from its west for one hundred and twenty years, until they plant palm trees [[Yaghrisu: to plant. The text here reads "yaghrisu al-nahl," literally "plant the palm trees" as transmitted.]].

And God knows best what is unseen.

Ibn 'Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr [[In K: Ibn Mas'ud.]] read ﴿yawma ta'ti﴾ with the feminine ta', like ﴿taltaqituhu ba'du al-sayyarah﴾ [[See vol. 9, p. 131.]]. Some of his fingers were cut off.

Jarir said:
When the news of al-Zubayr arrived, the streets of Medina humbled themselves, and the humbled mountains.
[[This describes the killing of al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, companion of the Messenger of God ﷺ, when he withdrew on the day of the Camel and was killed on the road by treachery.]]

Al-Mubarrad said: the feminine form here is by proximity to a feminine noun, not in accordance with the original form. Ibn Sirin read ﴿la tanfa'u﴾ with the ta'. Abu Hatim said: They mention that this was an error by Ibn Sirin. Al-Nahhas said: In this there is a subtle point of grammar, which Sibawayh mentioned, and it is that faith and the soul each include the other, so he made faith feminine since it comes from the soul and belongs to it. Sibawayh recited:

They walked as spear shafts quiver, their tips swayed by the passing of the gusting winds.
[[The verse is by Dhu al-Rummah, describing women: when they walk they sway, and their graceful turning is like upright spears that the winds move and bend.]]

Al-Mahdawi said: Very often they make the verb of a masculine mudaf (genitive-construct noun) feminine when its mudaf ilayhi (the noun it is annexed to) is feminine, and when the mudaf is part of that mudaf ilayhi, or belongs to it. On this is the verse of Dhu al-Rummah: "They walked..." (the whole line), where he made al-marr (the passing) feminine because it is annexed to al-riyah (the winds), which are feminine, since the marr is one of the winds.

Al-Nahhas said: There is another opinion on this, namely that al-iman (faith) is made feminine because it is a verbal noun (masdar), just as a feminine verbal noun may be made masculine, as in ﴿فَمَنْ جاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾ (So whoever receives an admonition from his Lord...) [see vol. 3, p. 359]. And as the poet said [the line is by Hatim and is in his Diwan and in Lisan al-Arab:
"Oh, my two beloved ones, the avoiding and the forsaking have strayed far,
and you have indeed excused me in seeking you, the excuse..."]:

"فَقَدْ عَذَرْتِنَا فِي صَحَابَتِهِ الْعُذْرَ"

So in one of the opinions he made al-udhr (the excuse) feminine because it carries the meaning of al-ma'dhirah (the excuse offered). ﴿قُلِ انْتَظِرُوا إِنَّا مُنْتَظِرُونَ﴾ (Say: Wait, indeed we are waiting), meaning: for the punishment to come upon you.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 159:

Ḥamzah and al-Kisa'i read (fāraqū [[from K.]]) with an alif, and this is the reading of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah honour his face, from al-mufāraqah and al-firāq (parting and separation), in the sense that they abandoned their religion and departed from it. ʿAlī used to say: "By Allah, they did not divide it (farraqūhu), but they parted from it (fāraqūhu)." The rest of the readers read it with tashdīd (farraqū), except al-Nakhaʿī, who read "farqū" without tashdīd, meaning they believed in some parts and disbelieved in others. The intended people are the Jews and the Christians, according to Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Suddi and al-Dahhak. They have been described as divided, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not divide except after clear evidence had come to them﴾ [[See vol. 20, p. 143.]], and He says: ﴿and they want to make distinction between Allah and His messengers﴾ [[See vol. 6, p. 5.]]. It was also said: he meant the polytheists, some of whom worshipped idols and some of whom worshipped the angels. It was also said: the verse is general concerning all disbelievers. And whoever innovates and brings what Allah the Mighty and Majestic has not commanded has divided his religion. Abu Hurayrah narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding this verse, "Indeed, those who divided their religion," that they are the people of innovations and doubtful matters, and the people of misguidance from this nation. Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated: Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj told us, Mujalid told us, from al-Sha'bi, from Shurayh, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to ʿĀ'ishah: "Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects (shiyaʿan), they are only the people of innovations, the people of desires, and the people of misguidance from this nation. O ʿĀ'ishah, indeed every person with a sin has repentance, except the people of innovations and the people of desires; for them there is no repentance. I am free of them, and they are free of us." Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated from Tawus, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited "Indeed, those who parted from their religion." The meaning of (shiyaʿan) is factions and parties. Every group whose affair is one, where some follow the opinion of others, are a shiyaʿ.

(You are not of them in anything) So he made his disassociation from them obligatory, and it is like the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: "Whoever cheats us is not of us," meaning we are free of him. The poet said:

*When you attempt treachery against Asad, / indeed I am not of you and you are not of me.* [[The verse is by al-Nabighah al-Dhubyani. He says this to ʿUyaynah ibn Hisn al-Fazari, who had invited him and his people to break off with Banu Asad and annul their alliance, but he refused and threatened them. He meant by treachery the breaking of the alliance (from Sharh al-Shawahid).]]

That is: I disassociate myself from you. The place of (fī shay'in) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl) of the pronoun in the predicate, as Abu ʿAli said. Al-Farra' said it is by omission of a noun, the meaning being: you are not of their punishment in anything; upon you is only the warning. [[In manuscript Z: "the conveyance (al-balagh)."]]

(Indeed their affair is with Allah) a consolation to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 160:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed﴾ is a beginning (mubtada'), and it is a conditional (shart), and the response (jawab) is (﻿﴿then he will have ten times the like of it﴾) — meaning, then he will have ten good deeds like it. The word "good deeds" (hasanat) has been omitted, and the "likes" (amthal), which are its attribute, have been placed in its position. Amthal is the plural of mithl. Sibawayh related: "ʿindi ʿashara nassabat," meaning "I have ten men who are genealogists (nassabat)." Abu ʿAli said: the feminine form is good in "ʿashru amthalihā" because amthal is added to a feminine noun, and when the addition is to a feminine noun which is itself that (i.e., the same in meaning), the feminine form is good in it, like "yaltaqitahu baʿḍu al-sayyarah" (some of the caravan will pick it up).

Some of his fingers were cut off [[In k: some of his companions.]]. Al-Hasan, Saʿid ibn Jubayr and al-Aʿmash read "fa-lahu ʿashru amthaliha." The implied meaning: for him are ten good deeds whose likes they are, i.e., for him, in reward, is ten times what is due to him. It is also possible that he has one like, and the like is multiplied so that it becomes ten. The "good deed" here is faith: whoever comes with the testimony that there is no god but Allah, for him, for every deed he did in the world of good, is ten times its reward.

(﻿﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed﴾) meaning shirk, (﻿﴿he will not be recompensed except with its like﴾) and that is eternal abiding in the Fire, because shirk is the greatest of sins and the Fire is the greatest of punishments. This is the saying of Exalted: ﴿a fitting recompense﴾, meaning a recompense that matches the deed. As for the good deed, it is different from that, by the explicit text of Allah, Exalted, concerning it. In a report: "The good deed is rewarded tenfold, and I add more; the evil deed is one, and I forgive; so woe to him whose single units outweigh his tens." Al-Aʿmash related from Abu Salih, who said: "The good deed is 'There is no god but Allah,' and the evil deed is shirk."

(﻿﴿And they will not be wronged﴾) meaning their reward for their deeds will not be diminished. The explanation of this verse has passed in al-Baqarah, and that it differs from spending in the way of Allah. For this reason some scholars said: the tenfold applies to the rest of the good deeds, and seven hundredfold to spending in the way of Allah, and the elite and the common are equal in this. Others said: the common folk have ten, and the elite have seven hundred and more, up to what cannot be counted, and this requires a textual report. The first view is more sound, due to the hadith of Khuraym ibn Fatik from the Prophet (ﷺ), in which: "As for a good deed for ten: whoever does a good deed, for him is ten times its like; and as for a good deed for seven hundred: spending in the way of Allah."

**First issue:** Al-Qurtubi's commentary on the Qur'an, *al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Qur'an*, on Surah 6, verses 161–163.

There are four issues (masa'il) in this passage.

**The first issue:** His saying, ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path﴾. When God the Exalted explained that the disbelievers had divided into factions, He explained that God had guided him (the Prophet) to the upright religion, which is the religion of Ibrahim. The word *dinan* (as a religion) is in the accusative as a state (ḥāl), according to Qutrub. It was also said that it is in the accusative governed by *hadani* (guided me), according to al-Akhfash.

Another (scholar) said: it is in the accusative by way of interpreting the meaning, because the meaning of *hadani* is "made me know a religion." It may also be a substitute (badal) for *al-sirat* (the path), meaning: He guided me to a straight path, a religion. It was also said: it is in the accusative by an implied verb, as if he said: "Follow a religion, and recognize a religion."

**(*Qiyaman*)** was read by the Kufans and Ibn Amir (in the other text: "and al-Kisa'i, but in al-Bahr the rest of the seven read *qiyaman* like *sayyid*"), with a kasra on the qaf, lightened, and a fatha on the ya, as a verbal noun (maṣdar) like *al-shiba'* (satiety), so it is described by it. The rest read it with a fatha on the qaf, a kasra on the ya, and shaddah (doubled), and both are dialect forms. The origin of the ya is the waw, *qayyum*, then the waw was assimilated into the ya, as in *mayyit*. Its meaning is: an upright religion with no crookedness in it.

**(*Millata Ibrahim*)** replaces *hanifan*. Al-Zajjaj said: it is a state (ḥāl) from Ibrahim. Ali ibn Sulayman said: it is in the accusative by an implied verb, "I mean" (a'nī).

**The second issue:** His saying, ﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer and my sacrifice﴾. The derivation of the word *ṣalāh* (prayer) has already been mentioned (see vol. 1, p. 168). It was said that the meaning of *ṣalāh* here is the night prayer, and it was said: the prayer of the Eid.

*Nusuk* is the plural of *nasīkah*, which is a sacrificed animal. Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others said the same. The meaning is: my slaughter during the Hajj and the 'Umrah.

Al-Hasan said: *nusuki* means my religion. Al-Zajjaj said: my worship, and from this comes *al-nasik*, the one who draws near to God through worship.

Some people said: *nusuk* in this verse means all righteous deeds and acts of obedience, from your saying: "So-and-so *nasaka*, so he is a *nasik*," meaning he worshipped.

**(*Wa mahyaya*)** means: what I do in my life. **(*Wa mamati*)** means: what I bequeath after my death. **Lillahi rabbi al-'alamin** means: I single Him out for drawing near to Him by these acts. It was also said: "*wa mahyaya wa mamati lillah*" means: my life and my death are for Him.

Al-Hasan read *nusuki* with the sin sukun. The people of Medina (read) *wa mahyay* with the ya sukun in continued recitation (idraj), while the common reading is with a fatha on it, because two sukun would come together. Al-Nahhas said: no grammarian permitted it except Yunus, and he permitted it because before it there is an alif, and the alif, the lengthening in it, stands in place of the vowel. Yunus permitted *iḍribani Zaydan* (strike them both, Zayd). The grammarians prohibited this because it joins two sukun where the second has no idgham (assimilation). Whoever recites with the recitation of the people of Medina and wishes to be free from error (laḥn) stops on *mahyay*, and so he is not making an error according to all the grammarians.

Ibn Abi Ishaq, Isa ibn Umar and Asim al-Jahdari read *wa mahyayya* with shaddah on the second ya, without an alif. This is the dialect of the upper Mudar, who say *qafayya* and *'asayya*. The lexicographers recited a line of verse:

*They outran my desire and went headlong after their own desires.*
*So they were snatched away, and every side has its place of death.*

This was already mentioned.

**The third issue:** Al-Kiya al-Tabari said: His saying, ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path﴾ up to His saying, ﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer and my sacrifice and my life and my death are for God, Lord of the worlds﴾. Al-Shafi'i used it as evidence for opening the prayer with this remembrance, since God commanded His Prophet ﷺ and revealed it in His Book. Then he mentioned the hadith of Ali (may God be pleased with him): that the Prophet ﷺ, when he began the prayer, would say: "I turned my face to Him who created the heavens and the earth, as a monotheist (ḥanīf), and I am not of the polytheists. Indeed my prayer and my sacrifice and my life and my death are for God, Lord of the worlds… and I am of the Muslims."

*(I say: Muslim related in his Sahih from Ali ibn Abi Talib, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, that when he stood for prayer he would say:)* "I turned my face to Him who created the heavens and the earth, as a monotheist, and I am not of the polytheists. Indeed my prayer and my sacrifice and my life and my death are for God, Lord of the worlds, without partner. And with that I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims. O God, You are the King; there is no god but You. You are my Lord and I am Your servant. I have wronged myself and acknowledged my sin, so forgive me all my sins, for none forgives sins but You. Guide me to the best of manners, for none guides to the best of them but You. Turn away from me the worst of them, for none turns away from me the worst of them but You. At Your service, and at Your pleasure; all good is in Your hands and evil is not attributed to You. You are blessed and exalted. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance." (The hadith.)

Al-Daraqutni related it and said at its end: It reached us from al-Nadr ibn Shumayl, who was among the scholars of language and other fields, that he said: The meaning of the words of the Messenger of God ﷺ, "and evil is not attributed to You," is: evil is not among the things by which one draws near to You.

Malik said: the opening supplication in prayer is not obligatory upon people, and what is obligatory upon them is the takbir, then the recitation. Ibn al-Qasim said: Malik did not hold that what people say before the recitation, "Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You," (is required). In the abridged work *Mukhtasar ma laysa fi al-Mukhtasar* it is stated that Malik used to say it for himself personally, because the hadith about it is sound, but he did not regard it for people, for fear that they would believe it obligatory.

Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi said: When I was young I used to pray behind our shaykh, the jurist Abu Bakr al-Dinawari, and once he saw me doing this and said: "My son, the jurists have differed on the obligation of reciting al-Fatiha behind the imam, but they have not differed that the opening supplication is a sunnah. So occupy yourself with what is obligatory and leave the sunan."

The proof for Malik is the Prophet's ﷺ saying to the Bedouin whom he taught prayer: "When you stand up for prayer, say takbir, then recite." He did not say to him "Glorify (sabbih)" as Abu Hanifa says, nor "Say: I turned my face," as al-Shafi'i says. He also said to Ubayy: "How do you recite when you begin the prayer?" He said: "I say: God is greatest, praise be to God, Lord of the worlds." He did not mention a turning (of the face) or glorification.

If it is said: Ali reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to say it. We say: it is possible that he said it before the takbir and then said takbir, and that is good according to us.

If it is said: al-Nasa'i and al-Daraqutni related that the Prophet ﷺ, when he began (*iftataḥa*) the prayer, would say takbir, then say: "Indeed my prayer and my sacrifice…" the hadith. We say: this we interpret as applying to voluntary prayer during the night, as came in the book of al-Nasa'i from Abu Sa'id, who said: "When the Messenger of God ﷺ began (*istaftaḥa*) the prayer at night, he would say: 'Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.'" Or (we interpret it) as applying to supererogatory prayer in general, for supererogatory prayer is lighter than the obligatory, since it is permissible to pray it standing, sitting, riding, and facing the qibla or not while traveling, so its ruling is easier.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 164:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: "Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, when He is the Lord of all things?"﴾ That is, its Owner. It is related that the disbelievers said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Return, O Muhammad, to our religion, worship our gods, and abandon what you are upon, and we will take upon ourselves for you every consequence you fear in your worldly life and in the Hereafter." So the verse was revealed. It is an interrogative that requires affirmation and rebuke. And "ghayra" is in the accusative governed by "abghi" (seek), and "rabban" is a specifier (tamyiz).

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And no soul earns [sin] except against itself﴾. In this there are two issues.

The first: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And no soul earns [sin] except against itself﴾. That is, your being upon that will not benefit me in seeking a lord other than Allah. "Except against itself" means that no one is held to account for the disobedience that another has committed and the sin that another has incurred.

The second: Some scholars among the dissenters have used this verse as evidence that the sale of a fudul (one who sells what he does not own) is not valid, and this is the view of al-Shafi'i. Our scholars (the Malikis) said: the intended meaning of the verse is the bearing of reward and punishment, not the worldly rulings, by the evidence of His saying, may He be exalted: "And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another" (Qur'an 6:164 in its continuation, as will come). The sale of the fudul, according to us, is suspended upon the approval of the owner; if he approves it, it is valid. This is ʿUrwah al-Bariqi, who sold and bought for the Prophet (ﷺ) and disposed of [property] without his command, and the Prophet (ﷺ) approved it. Abu Hanifa also held this view.

Al-Bukhari and al-Daraqutni related from ʿUrwah ibn Abi al-Ja'd, who said: A caravan of livestock (jalab) [[al-Jalab (with a fatha on the lam): what a people bring of sheep and other animals.]] was presented to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he gave me a dinar and said: "O ʿUrwah, go to the caravan and buy us a sheep with this dinar." So I went to the caravan, bargained, and bought two sheep for a dinar. I came driving them—or he said leading them—and a man met me on the way and bargained with me, so I sold him one of the two sheep for a dinar, and I brought the other sheep and the dinar. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is the sheep and this is your dinar." He said: "How did you do it?" So I related the account to him. He said: "O Allah, bless him in the transaction of his right hand." He said: "I have seen myself standing in the market (kunasa) [[its location in Kufa, which resembles being a market.]] of Kufa, and I would earn forty thousand before reaching my family." This is the wording of al-Daraqutni. Abu ʿUmar said: this is a good hadith, and in it is the authenticity of the Prophet's (ﷺ) approval of the two sheep; had that not been so, he would not have taken the dinar nor allowed the sale. In it is evidence for the permissibility of agency (wakalah), and there is no disagreement among scholars regarding it. If the principal (al-muwakkil) says to his agent: "Buy such-and-such," and he buys more than what he was commissioned for, does that command bind [the principal] or not? For example, a man says to another: "Buy with this dirham a pound of meat of such-and-such a description," and he buys four pounds of that description with that dirham. The view of Malik and his companions is that all of it binds him if it matches the description and is of its kind, because he is a doer of good (muhsin). This is also the view of Abu Yusuf and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan. Abu Hanifa said: the excess belongs to the buyer. And this hadith is a proof against him.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾. That is, no burden-carrier carries another's load; no soul is taken to account for another's sin, but rather every soul is held to account for its own crime and punished for its own sin. The root of "wizr" is weight, and from it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We removed from you your burden﴾ [[see vol. 20, p. 105.]]. Here it means sin, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And they will carry their burdens upon their backs﴾. This has already passed [[see vol. 6, pp. 413 and 342.]]. Al-Akhfash said: it is said "wazira yawzaru," "wazara yaziru," and "wuzira yuwzaru wazaran." And "izran" is permissible, as one says "isadah" (in the sense of wisadah).

The verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, who used to say: "Follow my way, and I will bear your burdens." This was related by Ibn ʿAbbas. It was also said that it was revealed in refutation of the Arabs in the Jahiliyyah, who held a man accountable for his father, his son, and the offense of his ally.

I say: It is possible that the intended meaning of this verse is in the Hereafter, and likewise the one before it. As for the worldly case, some of them may be held accountable for the crime of others, especially when the obedient do not forbid the disobedient, as has passed in the hadith of Abu Bakr concerning his saying: "You are responsible for yourselves" [[see vol. 6, pp. 413 and 342.]]. And His saying, may He be exalted: "And beware of a trial that will not strike exclusively those of you who have wronged" [[see p. 391 of this part.]]. "Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves" [[see vol. 9, p. 291.]]. Zaynab bint Jahsh said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we be destroyed while there are righteous people among us?" He said: "Yes, when wickedness (al-khabath) increases." The scholars said: its meaning is the children of fornication. And "al-khabath" (with a fatha on the ba') is the name for fornication. So Allah, may He be exalted, obligated through the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ) the blood money for manslaughter upon the paternal relatives ('aqilah), so that the blood of a free Muslim person would not be wasted, as a glorification of blood. The scholars unanimously agreed on this without any disagreement among them, which indicates what we have said.

It may also be that this refers to the worldly life: that Zayd is not held accountable for the act of ʿAmr, and that every direct perpetrator of a crime bears its consequence.

Abu Dawud related from Abu Rimthah, who said: I set out with my father toward the Prophet (ﷺ). Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said to my father: "Is this your son?" He said: "Yes, by the Lord of the Ka'bah." He said: "Truly?" He said: "I testify to it." He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) smiled, laughing at the firmness [of the resemblance] of my likeness to my father, and at my father's oath concerning me. Then he said: "As for him, he does not commit crime against you, and you do not commit crime against him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾.

What we have said at first is not contradicted by His saying: ﴿And they will surely carry their burdens and burdens along with their burdens﴾ [[see vol. 13, p. 330 and p. 12.]], for this is clarified in another verse, His saying: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾ [[see vol. 10, p. 96.]]. Whoever is a leader in misguidance, calls to it, and is followed in it, he bears the burden of whoever he misled without any reduction from the burden of the misleader, as will be explained, Allah willing.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 6, verse 165:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is He who has made you successors (khala'if) of the earth﴾. *Khala'if* is the plural of *khalifa*, as *karaim* is the plural of *karima*. Anyone who comes after those who have passed away is a *khalifa*, meaning He has made you successors to the earlier nations and the bygone generations. Al-Shammakh said:

*"The fates strike them, and they miss me, and I succeed (akhlufu) in abodes after abodes."*

﴿And He raised some of you above others﴾ in creation, provision, strength, expansiveness, virtue and knowledge.

﴿In degrees﴾ (*darajat*) is in the accusative because the preposition has been dropped; the meaning is "to degrees."

﴿That He may test you﴾ (*liyabluwakum*) is in the accusative by the *lam* of purpose (*lam kay*). *Ibtila'* (testing) means examination, i.e., that He may manifest from you what has as its outcome reward and punishment. He has always been self-sufficient in His knowledge. So He tests the wealthy with riches and asks them for gratitude, and He tests the poor with poverty and asks them for patience. It is also said that *"liyabluwakum"* means that some of you are tested by others, as He said: ﴿And We have made some of you a trial for others﴾, as will be explained in its place.

Then He warned them, saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment﴾ for whoever disobeys Him.

﴿And indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ to whoever obeys Him. He said "swift in punishment" together with describing Himself, glory be to Him, as one who gives respite, and although the punishment of the Fire is in the Hereafter, because everything that is coming is near, He is swift in this sense. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the matter of the Hour is but as a glance of the eye, or it is nearer﴾. And He said: ﴿They see it as distant, but We see it as near﴾.

It may also mean that He is swift in punishing whoever deserves it in this worldly life, so that the warning against committing sin is in this respect. And Allah knows best.

*The Surah of al-An'am is completed, by the praise of Allah, exalted is He, and His blessings and peace upon Muhammad (ﷺ), and upon his family and companions, with abundant peace.* [From manuscript K.]
